newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swap - Steady on lack of fresh factors.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swap - Steady on lack of fresh factors.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps at midday on Monday hovered around its Friday's quotes but surplus supplies continue to bear down levels, brokers and traders said.
July paper was last quoted $23.05/$23.40 per barrel within Friday's range of $23.15/$23.25.
Unsold prompt supplies continue to depress prices, traders said.
They cited the ample supplies in the cash market that were offered on Friday.
Late Friday, at least four sellers emerged to offer cargoes for loading between end June and early July but only one bid was seen.
"Stocks are incredibily high at this moment," said one trader.
Gas oil stocks in Singapore at over 11 million barrels are at their highest since at least Janaury 1994.
But some traders were more optimistic. They said firm crude values may support levels.
Short-covering ahead of the expiry of the July contract caused IPE Brent futures to close 26 cents higher from its previous settlement.
July Brent was last traded at $17.70 a barrel. August was last quoted on Simex at $17.70/$17.90, sideways from its last London closed at $17.76.
Fuel oil swaps were also little moved at $100.00/$101.00, with the market split between bulls and bears.
While supplies from the mideast is tightening during the summer season, demand was also sluggish, traders said.
